analysis:
The only change in this PR is a documentation row added to the environment-variable table in docs/provider/cli-reference.md, near head line 1751. It documents DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP, with source ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift (`shapeWarmupEnvironmentKey`). `0` disables the load-time shape warmup and `always` skips the shader-cache probe. The supplied head text covers only lines 1-830, so the changed row itself was not visible and I reviewed it only through the patch excerpt. The visible text is unchanged context, which I read for threat-model consistency.

Security relevance: the variable is a performance and warmup knob. Nothing in the evidence suggests it touches keys, attestation, encryption, coordinator authorization, the prefix-cache gate (T-041, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE semantics), logout or the App Attest worker. A warmup that runs a synthetic one-token decode or shader compilation could in principle interact with prefix-cache donation or timing (T-041 / SEC-035). The Swift implementation is not supplied, so I cannot verify that a warmup does not populate the SSD prefix cache or retain synthetic or plaintext data. The documentation change by itself makes no security claim and introduces no new attack surface. The environment variable is forwarded into launchd only by the operator, so it is local operator-controlled configuration and is within the existing operator-trust model (TB-003).

Remaining integration questions: whether ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift's warmup path stays isolated from the SSD prefix-cache donation path and from request data, and whether `always` or `0` changes any fail-closed behavior. These need the code change, which is not in this batch. No findings.
